result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make the declined card the only loud banner and explain why: it has a deadline and a consequence. Both give it a single 'Update card' button, keep the screen usable, and handle the Portuguese notice and the N tip differently from each other. B is slightly more useful as a developer handoff: its summary table has columns for dismissal and action, and it adds auto-expiry, aria-keyshortcuts and shortcut-safety details. B's placement for the Portuguese notice is a little indecisive: it lists a notice below the banner first, then says a tooltip is best. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers meet every rubric item. Each makes the declined-card message the only loud, non-dismissible banner with a single 'Update card' action, and treats the Portuguese notice and the N tip differently from each other. B is slightly better as a developer handoff: it says what to do when all three messages apply at once, hides the announcement while the card banner is showing, and gives more accurate ARIA advice. A's extra details (aria-keyshortcuts, auto-expire, shortcut safety) are useful, but its placement options for the Portuguese notice are less decisive.
